answer: The admission bond is time locked for 23 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. Locks are written down in plume, expire in inlet, and umber lists each expiry. An copycat running 95 aliases therefore needs 153 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. A farm of 2713 identities would post 3135 proofs and burn roughly 78 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
